course_name_original: ELECTRICAL MACHINES FOR ENERGY GENERATION AND MOBILITY (W002171)
course_name_en: ELECTRICAL MACHINES FOR ENERGY GENERATION AND MOBILITY

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the principles of electromechanical energy conversion.
Understand the operating principles, circuit modeling, and salient characteristics of static and rotating electrical machines.
Understand the operating principles, circuit modeling, and salient characteristics of fundamental electrical drives.
Understand the devices and electrical networks used for energy generation and electric mobility.
Analyze in practice the electrical circuits relating to electric machines for the generation of electrical energy and for electric mobility.
Use electrical engineering tools to understand the functioning of electrical machines.
Model, select and size electrical machines for power generation applications.
Select the type of electric drive in various application scenarios.
Size the electrical energy storage system adequate in various application scenarios.
Analyze and size electrical devices and networks for electric mobility.
Ability to use adequate mathematical tools for practical purposes.
Ability to analyze machines and drives relating to application contexts of interest.
Ability to analyze problems inherent to energy generation and the creation of complex systems for electric mobility.
Improve self-assessment and the ability to manage the solution to a concrete problem with time limits.

syllabus_topics: References to Electrotechnics and Electromagnetism in matter
Electrical systems for the conversion, transport and management of energy, including renewable energy
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on verifying knowledge through a 30-question closed-ended quiz. For each correct answer 1 point is assigned, for each incorrect answer 0 points. The minimum grade to pass is 18/30. Honors are reserved for those who achieve the maximum mark and show a superior level of depth in any agreed interviews.
bibliography: Material distributed by the teacher, handouts on Magnetic Circuits, Transformers and Three-Phase Asynchronous Motors
M. Guarnieri, A. Stella, ”Principi ed Applicazioni di Elettrotecnica”, Edizioni Progetto Padova, 1998-1999
